about: Which of Betterleaks' high-confidence rules (betterleaks-rules.json) detect secrets, edited by hand. Only rules under enabled are used. Every high-confidence rule is listed under enabled or excluded, with the reason, so a sync that brings a new rule fails the tests until it is decided here; it never turns on by itself.

excluded.adobe-client-id: a public identifier, not a secret: shipped in client code or used only to name an account
excluded.aikido-client-id: an identifier Betterleaks reports only beside the secret it belongs to (componentOnly), not a secret
excluded.algolia-application-id: an identifier Betterleaks reports only beside the secret it belongs to (componentOnly), not a secret
excluded.alibaba-access-key-id: an identifier Betterleaks reports only beside the secret it belongs to (componentOnly), not a secret
excluded.alibaba-secret-key: its keywords include secret and key, so without the Alibaba key id Betterleaks requires next to it, it matches any secret assignment; secret-assignment covers those at medium
excluded.alibaba-sts-access-key-id: an identifier Betterleaks reports only beside the secret it belongs to (componentOnly), not a secret
excluded.alibaba-sts-access-key-secret: its keywords include secret and key, so without the Alibaba key id Betterleaks requires next to it, it matches any secret assignment; secret-assignment covers those at medium

excluded.curl-auth-header: auth-header covers a credential header in curl -H and elsewhere; this rule's nested [^\n]*? loops backtrack polynomially in JavaScript (1.8 s on a 4 KB curl line holding carriage returns)
excluded.curl-auth-user: curl-user-password covers curl -u with its quoting, line continuations and placeholders; this rule loses its placeholder filter and would redact the user name with the password
